# Temperature Converter - Java Application
[![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen)]() [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-25%25-yellow)]() [![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-17-orange)]() [![Maven](https://img.shields.io/badge/Maven-3.9.6-blue)]() [![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-enabled-2496ED)]()
A Java application for converting temperatures between Fahrenheit, Celsius, and Kelvin, with complete CI/CD pipeline support.
## Features
- ✅ **Temperature Conversions** - Fahrenheit ↔ Celsius - Kelvin → Celsius - Extreme temperature detection (-40°C to 50°C)
- ✅ **Testing & Quality** - 7 comprehensive unit tests - JaCoCo code coverage reporting - JUnit 5 test framework
- ✅ **CI/CD Pipeline** - Jenkins automation - Docker containerization - Automated testing and reporting
## Project Information
### GitHub Repository - **URL**: https://github.com/YingLuo0208/temperature-converter-java - **Branch**: main - **Author**: YingLuo (YingLuo0208)
### Docker Hub - **Username**: luoying0208 - **Repository**: luoying0208/temperature-converter - **Tag**: v1 - **Pull**: `docker pull luoying0208/temperature-converter:v1`
## Quick Start
### Prerequisites
- Java 17 or higher - Maven 3.6+ - Docker (optional, for containerization) - Jenkins (optional, for CI/CD)
### Clone Repository
```bash git clone https://github.com/YingLuo0208/temperature-converter-java.git cd temperature-converter-java ```
### Build and Run
```bash # Build the project mvn clean package
# Run the application java -jar target/temperature-converter.jar ```
**Expected Output:** ``` === Temperature Converter Demo ===
Fahrenheit to Celsius: 100.0°F = 37.78°C
Celsius to Fahrenheit: 25.0°C = 77.00°F
Kelvin to Celsius: 300.0K = 26.85°C
Temperature Check: 60.0°C is EXTREME
=== Conversion Complete === ```
## Local Development
### Run Tests
```bash # Run all tests mvn test
# Run with coverage report mvn clean test jacoco:report ```
### View Coverage Report
After running tests, open the coverage report: ```bash # Windows start target/site/jacoco/index.html
# macOS/Linux open target/site/jacoco/index.html ```
## Docker Usage
### Build Docker Image
```bash docker build -t temperature-converter:v1 . ```
### Run Docker Container
```bash # Run once and remove docker run --rm temperature-converter:v1
# Run with custom name docker run --name temp-converter temperature-converter:v1 ```
### Push to Docker Hub
```bash # Login to Docker Hub docker login
# Tag the image docker tag temperature-converter:v1 luoying0208/temperature-converter:v1
# Push to Docker Hub docker push luoying0208/temperature-converter:v1 ```
### Pull from Docker Hub
```bash docker pull luoying0208/temperature-converter:v1 docker run --rm luoying0208/temperature-converter:v1 ```
## Jenkins CI/CD
### Pipeline Configuration
The project includes a complete Jenkinsfile with the following stages:
1. **Checkout** - Clone from Git 2. **Build** - Maven compile 3. **Run Tests** - Execute unit tests 4. **Generate JaCoCo Report** - Code coverage 5. **Publish Test Results** - JUnit reports 6. **Publish Coverage Report** - JaCoCo reports 7. **Build Docker Image** - Create container 8. **Push Docker Image** - Upload to Docker Hub
### Jenkins Setup
#### 1. Prerequisites - Jenkins with the following plugins: - Maven Integration Plugin - Docker Pipeline Plugin - JaCoCo Plugin - JUnit Plugin
#### 2. Configure Maven - Go to **Manage Jenkins** → **Global Tool Configuration** - Add Maven installation with name: `Maven3`
#### 3. Add Docker Hub Credentials - Go to **Manage Jenkins** → **Manage Credentials** - Add credentials: - **Kind**: Username with password - **Username**: luoying0208 (your Docker Hub username) - **Password**: Your Docker Hub password/token - **ID**: `Docker_Hub`
#### 4. Create Pipeline Job - Click **New Item** - Enter name: `temperature-converter-pipeline` - Select **Pipeline** - In Pipeline section: - **Definition**: Pipeline script from SCM - **SCM**: Git - **Repository URL**: https://github.com/YingLuo0208/temperature-converter-java.git - **Branch**: main - **Script Path**: Jenkinsfile - Save and run!
### Environment Variables
The Jenkinsfile uses the following configuration:
```groovy DOCKERHUB_CREDENTIALS_ID = 'Docker_Hub' DOCKERHUB_REPO = 'luoying0208/temperature-converter' DOCKER_IMAGE_TAG = 'v1' GIT_REPO = 'https://github.com/YingLuo0208/temperature-converter-java.git' ```
## Testing
### Test Coverage
Current test coverage: - **Lines**: 25% - **Methods**: 83% (5/6 methods) - **Classes**: 100%
### Test Cases
The project includes 7 comprehensive test methods:
1. `testFahrenheitToCelsius()` - 7 test cases 2. `testCelsiusToFahrenheit()` - 8 test cases 3. `testIsExtremeTemperature()` - 17 test cases 4. `testKelvinToCelsius()` - 7 test cases 5. `testRoundTripConversion()` - Conversion accuracy tests 6. `testExtremeTemperatureWithConversion()` - Combined tests 7. `testNegativeZeroAndPositiveZero()` - Edge cases
## Project Structure
``` temperature-converter-java/ ├── src/ │ ├── main/ │ │ └── java/ │ │ └── TemperatureConverter.java # Main application class │ └── test/ │ └── java/ │ └── TemperatureConverterTest.java # Unit tests ├── target/ │ ├── temperature-converter.jar # Executable JAR │ └── site/jacoco/ # Coverage reports ├── Dockerfile # Docker configuration ├── Jenkinsfile # CI/CD pipeline ├── pom.xml # Maven configuration ├── .dockerignore # Docker build exclusions ├── .gitignore # Git ignore rules ├── docker-build.bat # Docker automation script ├── git-push.bat # Git push automation script └── README.md # This file ```
## Code Quality
### Quality Metrics
- ✅ All 7 tests passing - ✅ No compilation errors - ✅ Clean build output - ✅ Executable JAR generated
## Troubleshooting
### Common Issues
#### 1. Maven Build Fails ```bash # Clean and rebuild mvn clean install
# Update dependencies mvn clean install -U ```
#### 2. Docker Build Fails ```bash # Check Docker is running docker --version
# Clean Docker cache docker system prune -a ```
#### 3. Jenkins Pipeline Fails - Verify Maven is configured as 'Maven3' - Check Docker Hub credentials ID is 'Docker_Hub' - Ensure Docker is accessible from Jenkins agent
